eyebrow: Docker & Deployment for AI Applications · Chapter One
subtitle: Lesson 3 · Docker Fundamentals

code:
FROM python:3.12-slim    # base image, always first
WORKDIR /app              # paths below are relative to this
COPY requirements.txt .   # bring a file in from your machine
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt  # runs at build time
ENV LOG_LEVEL=info        # set an environment variable
EXPOSE 8000                # documents the port, doesn't open it
CMD ["python", "server.py"]  # runs when a container starts
caption: One instruction per line, executed in order. FROM always comes first.

code:
# Good: dependencies change rarely, stays cached
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY . .          # app code changes often, only this re-runs

# Bad: any code change invalidates pip install too
COPY . .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
caption: Put what changes least at the top of the file.

code:
CMD ["python", "server.py"]
# docker run my-app                  -> python server.py
# docker run my-app python debug.py  -> python debug.py (replaced)

ENTRYPOINT ["python", "server.py"]
# docker run my-app --port 9000      -> python server.py --port 9000
caption: CMD is a default you can override. ENTRYPOINT is fixed; args get appended.

code:
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
ENV LOG_LEVEL=info
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["python", "server.py"]
caption: Eight lines, seven instructions, each doing exactly what its name says.
